text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash you're experiencing, including where it started and when you first noticed it? Also, have you had any recent fever, joint pain, or changes in your energy levels?

speaker: Doctor
text: When exactly did the cough and joint pain begin relative to the rash, and what specific medication was your new provider prescribe for your arthritis? Do you have any known drug allergies or a history of asthma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of your sudden rash, mucositis, cough, and recent new arthritis medication is concerning for a severe drug reaction. Did the rash begin shortly after you started the new medication, and have you noticed any blisters or peeling skin? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Normal. Skin Biopsy Findings: Epidermal necrosis and detachment, consistent with severe drug reaction. Vital Signs: Temperature 37.5°C (99.5°F), Blood Pressure 127/68 mmHg, Heart Rate 125 bpm, Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min, Oxygen Saturation 98% on room air. Skin Examination: Coalescing erythematous macules, bullae, and desquamation localized to the upper half of the back; ulcers and erythema present in oropharynx.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the biopsy results showing epidermal necrosis and your symptoms of mucositis and blistering, you are likely suffering from Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. Did you notice any specific new medication, particularly an antibiotic or anticonvulsant, started within the last few weeks prior to these symptoms?
